[NFCT.2.1] Asserting is how a fact enters working memory. The call takes the
schema the fact is an instance of, the values that fill its slots, and how many
there are.

The values are **positional**: the i-th value fills the i-th slot the schema
declared ([NFCT.1.4.1]). A value carries no name, so position is the only thing
that could bind it to a slot -- which is why the count must equal the schema's
slot count exactly ([NFCT.2.2]), and why each value's kind is checked against
the type declared *at that position* ([NFCT.2.3]). An integrator assembling
values from a keyed source is the one responsible for ordering them.

Nothing the caller passes is retained. Every buffer reachable from the values
is borrowed for the duration of the call ([NFCT.2.4]), and the optional
out-parameter is the only thing that outlives it ([NFCT.2.5]).

Asserting also fires nothing. The fact lands in working memory and whatever it
activates waits on the agenda until the engine is pumped ([NLFC.2.1]).
